findings.observation: The dedicated Agent destination is hidden behind the existing top-left orb with no visible text cue on Today, so a busy recruiter must already understand that the orb now means Agent configuration rather than only workspace utilities.
findings.evidence: Frozen scope: docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-agent-crm-redesign/scope.md; Today entry screenshot docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-agent-crm-redesign/screenshots/01-today-entry.png; entry wiring and accessibility label in apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter who does not explore the orb may miss where Memory, imports, and permissions live, which slows setup and weakens the product's new CRM identity.
findings.recommendation: Add one lightweight onboarding cue or first-run coach mark anchored to the orb, then remove it after dismissal so the steady-state UI stays quiet.
findings.verification: In a first-run usability pass, 5 of 5 target users should reach Agent settings from Today without verbal prompting in under 10 seconds.

findings.observation: The Sources & imports screen distinguishes available and planned capabilities well, but it does not show freshness, last review time, or any explicit health detail for the live configuration states shown there.
findings.evidence: Sources screenshot docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-agent-crm-redesign/ui-test-attachments/E66EFB07-7D49-40B9-B3D5-82CBCAC367F1.png; source summary and row content in apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAgentStudioView.swift; scenario goal in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-agent-crm-redesign/scope.md.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can see whether a capability is available or planned, but cannot quickly tell whether an existing setup is current, stale, or last checked, which matters when trusting future imports or outbound effects.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact last-reviewed or status-detail line for configured sources and outbound projections without increasing the number of first-level rows.
findings.verification: After enabling a source in preview or test data, the Sources screen should show a reproducible timestamp or freshness label that changes after configuration updates.

findings.observation: This slice clearly frames planned imports as non-interactive roadmap items, but it stops at capability orientation and does not yet let the recruiter start a governed import review from the same destination.
findings.evidence: Planned import cards marked Planned in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-agent-crm-redesign/ui-test-attachments/E66EFB07-7D49-40B9-B3D5-82CBCAC367F1.png; intentional limits in docs/evaluations/2026-09-03-agent-crm-redesign/scope.md.
findings.user_impact: The screen is strong as a clean control plane, but it does not yet reduce manual setup work for imports beyond explanation, so the recruiter value is still preparatory rather than time-saving.
findings.recommendation: Make the next slice start a staged import review from this page for one source only, ideally Contacts/vCard/CSV, with duplicate review and import receipt.
findings.verification: A recruiter should be able to begin one import from Agent, review proposed fields, confirm, and see a completion receipt without leaving the control plane.

strengths: The dedicated Agent destination stays out of Today and preserves the product's existing attention surfaces, which keeps the core workspace from becoming a cluttered dashboard.
The first level is appropriately sparse for a time-constrained recruiter: exactly Memory, About you, Sources & imports, and Action permissions.
The screen avoids agent theater. It gives the Agent an identity and editable alias without fake autonomy, streaks, or chat metrics.
The source design is honest about platform reality: LinkedIn is a profile reference only, while future imports are shown as planned and non-live.
Consequential actions remain clearly gated by approval, which protects operational trust while still making Action Button and Calendar capabilities reachable.
missing_evidence: No field evidence from real recruiters shows whether the orb-based Agent entry is discoverable enough without onboarding support.
No executable proof in the frozen artifact covers return-after-a-day behavior, stale source messaging, or interrupted setup recovery for the Agent destination.
No comparative time-to-complete data shows that this configuration model is faster or clearer than the prior menu-based setup path.
open_questions: Should the orb keep dual semantics permanently, or should the legacy workspace menu eventually be separated from Agent identity now that configuration moved here?
Which single import source should become the first executable staged flow from this page: LinkedIn archive, Contacts/vCard, or CSV?
Does the product want a recruiter-visible freshness model for sources and memory, and if so should it surface on the first row or only inside each detail screen?
